note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 85; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 54) on data/benches/spectra.json: atomic spectra of four discharge lamps through the spectral viewer; hydrogen's Balmer lines and the Rydberg constant.
title: Experiment: atomic spectra

report.label: hydrogen's red line, H-alpha
report.why: NIST: 656.279 nm in air (from n = 3 to 2). The viewer reads to the nanometre.

report.label: hydrogen's blue-green line, H-beta
report.why: NIST: 486.135 nm in air (from n = 4 to 2).

report.label: the Rydberg constant
report.why: 1/lambda = R (1/4 - 1/n^2): from H-alpha, R = 1 / (lambda (1/4 - 1/9)); from H-beta, R = 1 / (lambda (1/4 - 1/16)). Hydrogen's own R is 1.09678e7 /m (a little under the infinite-mass 1.09737e7: the nucleus moves too); wavelengths in air are 0.03 % short of those in vacuum.

report.label: the lamp with a green line at 546 nm
report.why: Mercury's green 546.07 nm, beside its violet 404.66 and blue 435.83: the lines of a fluorescent tube's mercury.

steps.title: The hydrogen lamp on
steps.text: Right-click the hydrogen lamp and drag its power up.

steps.title: The probe on its tube
steps.text: Drag the viewer's probe from its holder onto the hydrogen lamp's glowing tube. Right-click the viewer: it lists the lines it sees. Hydrogen's red line is H-alpha, its blue-green H-beta: wait while the viewer reads every nanometre.

checks.text: the probe on the hydrogen lamp

steps.why: A hydrogen atom's electron falling to its second level gives Balmer's lines: from the third, H-alpha (656 nm), from the fourth H-beta (486), the fifth H-gamma (434), the sixth H-delta (410).

steps.title: Its lines in the notebook
steps.text: Right-click the viewer: when it has read every nanometre it lists the lines it sees. In the notebook write lambda = hydrogen's red line's wavelength (H-alpha), then lambda = its blue-green's (H-beta).
